title: Of Wyrms and Drakes
author: Brother Cuthwin, Collegium
pages: Bestiary, ninth leaf. Of the great wyrms few remain, and each is a country to itself. A wise reeve knows whose country his village stands in, and knows the signs before the wings.
Cindermaw, the red, sleeps beneath the Anvil Peaks on the gold of fallen Varnkhar. Before he wakes, hot springs boil, sulphur rides the wind, and goats come down from the heights in daylight.
Rimeback, the white, hunts the Reach in winter. Frost in high summer is her warning. Deer found frozen standing are her larder. Fire troubles her more than steel. Light the beacons.
Sorrowscale, the Mire-Mother, breeds fen-drakes in the Murk. When the frogs stop singing and the skrell grow suddenly polite, count your cattle at dusk and keep the children inside.
Lesser drakes, dog-sized to horse-sized, hunt in flights. They take sheep and set ricks alight. Burnt hay with no lightning, and tracks that end in the middle of a field, mean drakes.
Tribute stones, where lords leave cattle for a wyrm, are shameful but old. A hunt costs lives. A wyrm-slayer may claim a crown. Choose knowing that every choice has a price.
